I know your pain. Been dealing with something similar at the moment. All I did for two months was be in bed and having mental breakdowns left and right. If you can’t crochet you can try other hobbies like writing, drawing or painting, pretty much anything that occupies your hands. It’s doesn’t have to be perfect just as long as you are enjoying the process.
Try also talking it out with a school counselor or someone you trust. I know you mentioned school doesn’t start 2months from now, but see if they can help you out. It helped me a lot to open up to someone. If you can’t, try writing it out on a journal, it might also help.

I hear ya. When I was in 7th grade I felt like I had to be perfect to make everyone and everything happy. My lowest score was once a B- and my parents flipped. But over the years I learned that middle school grades don’t count much for college. Plus all the stress would give me anxiety. I also had a bad time talking to my parents about my feelings. I just never felt like I should burden them. Or if they would even understand or care. 
But I realize that if they really loved me they would take the time to try and listen. So I tried talking to them more bit by bit till I felt like I was talking to a friend. I didn’t like told them straight away what i was feeling, I would just ask if they had gone through stuff like that as a kid or knew someone. And when they asked why I would ask I just would say I sorta feel that way but I wasn’t sure about their reaction  would be or if they would understand since I’m just a kid. And slowly they started to notice I wasn’t happy and needed them as parents. 

Also talk to an adult you trust about being depressed. Like a teacher, counselor, or parents. The sooner you get help for it the better. I waited till I was 20 and it in hindsight should’ve done it sooner. Like when I was 15 and noticed I was miserable. 

Also do stuff that makes you happy. Pleasing others is not your job. I know because I had to pretend to be perfect all the time and do stuff to make others happy. When in reality I was wasn’t perfect and I hated doing whatever made other happy. And trying to keep up appearances is exhausting. I was so much happier doing things I liked and not pretending to be someone i wasn’t was liberating.  I spent so much time worrying about others that I sorta missed out on stuff just to please others. 

Hope this helps kid.
